notes: Edit chosen for relation-property coverage: it moves Siemens from one class (DAX members) to another (CAC 40 members), so it carries ABox inheritance (the CAC 40 class rule: every member is listed on Euronext Paris), and `index_constituent_of` carries the role chain `chain:subindex_of->index_constituent_of` (new in relations/finance.md), which with 'every CAC 40 stock is in the SBF 120' gives the second determinate query. Both discriminate: Siemens left the Paris Bourse in December 2003 and is in no French index. The inheritance query uses the rule that finance-replace-0008 edits; it is a bridge here, not an edit, so Rule 4 is not affected. R1: Siemens has been a DAX member continuously since 1988 (no date dependence in practice); its headquarters (Munich and Berlin) is not used. Derivability unlikely (stored). Worlds: Siemens's Frankfurt listing is stored by name (w1) or reached only through its index (w2: a DAX company's home market is Frankfurt). w1 is consistent: CAC 40 members can have their primary listing elsewhere and add a Paris line (Stellantis, ArcelorMittal, Airbus are multi-listed). w2 contradicts no firm fact outside the chain. w2 is the less likely world (Siemens's Frankfurt listing is well known), but Decision 4 keeps lopsided worlds. 'Is Siemens listed on Euronext Paris?' is determinate: w1 has a Paris listing as well, w2 has Paris as home. Near query: Toyota's index (the Nikkei 225) shares the relation and differs from the new value. Inverse ('counts ... among its constituents') is in the paraphrase. Determinate queries: inheritance and chain.
